intensity-domain.short: A band of intensities in which the body responds in the same typical way: moderate, heavy, severe or extreme. The bands are set by your own thresholds, not by a fixed % of maximum.

moderate-domain.short: Efforts below the first lactate threshold (or gas exchange threshold). Oxygen uptake settles within a few minutes and blood lactate stays near resting values.

severe-domain.short: Efforts above critical power. Oxygen uptake climbs to its maximum and lactate keeps rising, so the effort ends within minutes: the harder, the sooner.

extreme-domain.short: Efforts so hard that you are exhausted before oxygen uptake can climb to its maximum: roughly all-out efforts shorter than about 2 minutes.

vo2-slow-component.short: A slow extra rise in oxygen uptake during hard constant-power exercise, after the first quick rise. Above critical power it carries oxygen uptake up to its maximum.

aerobic-threshold.short: An older name for the first lactate threshold (LT1): the intensity where blood lactate first rises above its resting level in a step test.

anaerobic-threshold.short: An older, misleading name for the second lactate threshold (LT2), where lactate starts to climb steeply. Muscles are not short of oxygen there; the name stuck from an early theory.

obla.short: The power or speed at which blood lactate reaches a fixed 4 mmol·L⁻¹ in a step test. Simple to read off the curve, but the same for everyone, so it fits some athletes badly.

dmax.short: A way to find a lactate threshold from the curve's shape: draw a straight line from the first to the last point of the step test; the threshold is the curve point farthest from that line.

maximal-metabolic-steady-state.short: The highest intensity at which oxygen uptake, blood lactate and muscle chemistry can still level off. Critical power and MLSS are two ways to estimate it.

critical-speed.short: The running (or swimming) form of critical power, in m·s⁻¹: the speed the speed–duration curve levels off at. Below it, running can settle into a steady state.

mcardle-disease.short: A rare inherited condition in which muscle cannot break down its glycogen. People with it make almost no lactate during exercise, which makes them a natural test of what lactate does.

talk-test.short: A field check of intensity: read or speak a short passage during exercise. 'Comfortable', 'not sure' and 'can't speak comfortably' mark rising intensities.

rpe.short: How hard an effort feels, scored on a scale, most often Borg's 6–20 scale (6 = no exertion, 20 = maximal).

hr-deflection-point.short: The point in a step test where heart rate stops rising in a straight line with speed or power. Conconi claimed it marked the lactate threshold; a later study in trained runners found it does not.
